title: 𝔽ₚ[ℤ/p] Is a Local Ring with Nilpotent Augmentation Ideal = Jacobson Radical
description: The full local-ring structure behind the modular failure of Maschke's theorem. The parent counterexample 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is not semisimple was witnessed by one nilpotent g − 1; here that element is shown to GENERATE the augmentation ideal (ker ε = (g − 1), the codimension-one ideal of coefficient-sum-zero elements), which is therefore principal and nilpotent of index ≤ p: (ker ε)^p = ⊥. The augmentation ideal is maximal (kernel of the surjection ε onto the field 𝔽_p) and contains every maximal ideal (it equals the nilradical), so 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is a LOCAL ring whose unique maximal ideal is exactly its Jacobson radical: Ring.jacobson A = ker ε ≠ ⊥. This nonvanishing radical yields an independent, radical-theoretic proof (via IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥ for Artinian rings) that the ring is not semisimple — the Artin–Wedderburn obstruction made explicit. Structurally 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] ≅ 𝔽_p[X]/((X−1)^p), the canonical local Artinian ring with nonzero nilpotent maximal ideal.

originalContributions: ker_eq_span: the augmentation ideal of 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is PRINCIPAL, generated by the nilpotent g − 1 — ker ε = (g − 1). Proved by MonoidAlgebra.induction_on: every element y satisfies y − (ε y)·1 ∈ (g − 1), because every group element is a power of the generator (of (ofAdd m) = g^(m.val)) and g − 1 ∣ gⁿ − 1 (sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow); this completes the parent's first open question (identify g − 1 as a generator of the augmentation ideal)

ker_pow_card: the augmentation ideal is NILPOTENT of index ≤ p — (ker ε)^p = ⊥, via Ideal.span_singleton_pow ((span {s})^n = span {sⁿ}) and (g − 1)^p = 0; the quantitative sharp nilpotency, strictly beyond the parent's element-level (g − 1)^p = 0

isLocalRing: 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is a LOCAL ring — its unique maximal ideal is the augmentation ideal. The ideal is maximal (kernel of the surjection ε onto the field 𝔽_p), and any maximal ideal contains the nilradical = (g − 1) = ker ε, so equality forces uniqueness (IsLocalRing.of_unique_max_ideal)
jacobson_eq_ker: the Jacobson radical EQUALS the augmentation ideal — Ring.jacobson A = ker ε, computed from the local structure (Ring.jacobson = maximalIdeal = ker ε)
jacobson_ne_bot: the Jacobson radical of 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is NONZERO — the precise Artin–Wedderburn obstruction to semisimplicity

not_isSemisimpleRing: an INDEPENDENT radical-theoretic proof that 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is not semisimple, via IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥ for Artinian rings — distinct from the parent's non-reduced route
ker_isMaximal / ε_surjective: the augmentation ε : 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] → 𝔽_p is surjective and its kernel is a maximal ideal (kernel of a surjection onto a field)

mathlibDependencies.description: For an Artinian ring, IsSemisimpleRing R ↔ Ring.jacobson R = ⊥; converts the nonzero Jacobson radical into the failure of semisimplicity.
In a local ring the Jacobson radical is the maximal ideal, and the kernel of a surjection onto a field is the maximal ideal; together they give Ring.jacobson A = ker ε.
Induction over group-algebra elements through of/add/smul; the engine for proving the augmentation ideal is principal.
(span {s})ⁿ = span {sⁿ} in a commutative ring; turns the element nilpotency (g − 1)^p = 0 into the ideal nilpotency (ker ε)^p = ⊥.

overview.historicalContext: Maschke's theorem (1899) makes the group algebra k[G] semisimple when char k ∤ |G|; Brauer's modular representation theory (from 1935) studies the opposite regime, char k = p ∣ |G|, where k[G] has a nonzero Jacobson radical and decomposes into blocks. The smallest witness is 𝔽_p[ℤ/p]. The parent entry certified non-semisimplicity through a single nilpotent; the present entry exhibits the complete local structure that the modular theory rests on. Via the isomorphism 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] ≅ 𝔽_p[X]/(X^p − 1) = 𝔽_p[X]/((X − 1)^p), the ring is the canonical example of a local Artinian (in fact a truncated-polynomial / chain) ring: a unique maximal ideal (X − 1) that is nonzero and nilpotent. That nonzero radical is precisely the Artin–Wedderburn obstruction that makes the group algebra non-semisimple, and it is the object whose study (the radical, its powers, the socle series) is the heart of modular representation theory.
overview.problemStatement: Let $p$ be prime and $A = \mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}/p]$. Show that the augmentation ideal $I = \ker(\varepsilon)$, where $\varepsilon : A \to \mathbb{F}_p$ sends $\sum a_g g \mapsto \sum a_g$, is principal and generated by $g - 1$; that it is nilpotent with $I^{p} = 0$; that $A$ is a local ring with $I$ as its unique maximal ideal; and that the Jacobson radical of $A$ equals $I$ and is nonzero, giving a radical-theoretic proof that $A$ is not semisimple.
overview.proofStrategy: First identify the augmentation ideal as principal. Every group element h = ofAdd m is a power of the generator, of h = g^(m.val) (of_eq_g_pow, via ofAdd_nsmul and ZMod.natCast_zmod_val), so of h − 1 is a multiple of g − 1 because g − 1 ∣ gⁿ − 1 (sub_dvd_pow_sub_pow). By MonoidAlgebra.induction_on this propagates to all elements: y − (ε y)·1 ∈ (g − 1) (sub_smul_one_mem). For y ∈ ker ε this gives y ∈ (g − 1), and conversely g − 1 ∈ ker ε, so ker ε = (g − 1) (ker_eq_span). Then (ker ε)^p = (span {g − 1})^p = span {(g − 1)^p} = span {0} = ⊥ by Ideal.span_singleton_pow and the Frobenius collapse (g − 1)^p = 0 (ker_pow_card). The augmentation ε is surjective (it retracts the unit 𝔽_p ↪ A), so its kernel is maximal (RingHom.ker_isMaximal_of_surjective onto the field 𝔽_p). Any maximal ideal M is prime and hence contains the nilradical, which contains the nilpotent g − 1, so ker ε = (g − 1) ⊆ M; maximality of ker ε forces M = ker ε, giving a unique maximal ideal and locality (IsLocalRing.of_unique_max_ideal). In a local ring Ring.jacobson = maximalIdeal = ker ε (jacobson_eq_ker), which is nonzero since it contains g − 1 ≠ 0 (jacobson_ne_bot). Finally, A is Artinian (finite), so IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥; the nonzero radical forbids semisimplicity (not_isSemisimpleRing).
keyInsights: The augmentation ideal is principal because the group is cyclic. Every basis element is a power g^k of the single generator, and the telescoping identity g − 1 ∣ g^k − 1 collapses the whole codimension-one ideal onto the single generator g − 1 — so ker ε = (g − 1), upgrading the parent's lone nilpotent into a complete description of the ideal it generates.

Nilpotency is sharp at the ideal level, not just the element level. The parent showed (g − 1)^p = 0; here (ker ε)^p = ⊥, i.e. the entire ideal is nilpotent of index ≤ p. This is what makes the radical computable: a nilpotent ideal sits inside the nilradical, and here it IS the nilradical and the Jacobson radical.

Locality comes for free once the ideal is principal and nilpotent. The augmentation ideal is maximal (its quotient is the field 𝔽_p) and, being nilpotent, lies in every prime — hence in every maximal — ideal; a maximal ideal contained in every maximal ideal is the only one. So 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is local, the modular analogue of the fact that for char k ∤ |G| the algebra is a product of fields/matrix rings.

The Jacobson radical IS the augmentation ideal, and its non-vanishing is the obstruction to semisimplicity. This gives a second, radical-theoretic proof of non-semisimplicity (through IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥) that is conceptually independent of the parent's 'a commutative semisimple ring is reduced' route, and it is the form that generalizes to arbitrary G with p ∣ |G|.

The structural slogan 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] ≅ 𝔽_p[X]/((X − 1)^p) is realized concretely: a local Artinian ring whose maximal ideal (X − 1) is nilpotent of index exactly p. Everything the modular theory needs — radical, radical powers, the length-p composition series of the regular module — is visible in this one principal ideal.

sections.title: Setup: the Modular Group Algebra, Generator, and Augmentation Map
sections.summary: Fixes a prime p and defines G = Multiplicative (ZMod p), A = 𝔽_p[ℤ/p], and the CharP (A p) p instance. Introduces the standard generator g = of (ofAdd 1) and the augmentation algebra map ε : A → 𝔽_p (MonoidAlgebra.lift of the trivial hom), with ε_of and ε_g recording ε(of a) = 1 and ε(g) = 1.

sections.title: The Generator and Its Nilpotent Difference
sections.summary: g_pow_card proves g^p = 1 (the exponent p • 1 = 0 in ZMod p). g_sub_one_pow_card applies the Frobenius collapse sub_pow_char to get (g − 1)^p = 0; isNilpotent_g_sub_one packages this nilpotency and g_sub_one_ne_zero shows g − 1 ≠ 0 (the generator differs from the identity).

sections.title: The Augmentation Ideal Is Principal: ker ε = (g − 1)
sections.summary: of_eq_g_pow identifies each basis element of (ofAdd m) with the power g^(m.val); of_sub_one_mem then shows of h − 1 ∈ (g − 1) via g − 1 ∣ gⁿ − 1. sub_smul_one_mem propagates 'y − (ε y)·1 ∈ (g − 1)' to all y by MonoidAlgebra.induction_on, yielding ker_eq_span: ker ε = (g − 1). ker_pow_card then gives the ideal nilpotency (ker ε)^p = ⊥ from span_singleton_pow.

sections.title: Maximality, Locality, and the Jacobson Radical
sections.summary: ε_surjective and ker_isMaximal make the augmentation ideal maximal (kernel of a surjection onto the field 𝔽_p); ker_ne_bot records it is nonzero. isLocalRing proves 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] local via of_unique_max_ideal (a maximal ideal contains the nilradical = (g − 1) = ker ε). jacobson_eq_ker computes Ring.jacobson A = ker ε, jacobson_ne_bot notes it is nonzero, and not_isSemisimpleRing concludes non-semisimplicity from the Artinian iff IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥.

openQuestions.question: Generalize the principal-and-nilpotent augmentation ideal to 𝔽_p[(ℤ/p)^n] and more generally to 𝔽_p[P] for a finite abelian p-group P: the augmentation ideal is the unique maximal ideal and is nilpotent, so the algebra is local. Determine the exact nilpotency index in terms of the group invariants.

For an arbitrary finite group G with p ∣ |G| (not necessarily a p-group), show Ring.jacobson (𝔽_p[G]) ≠ ⊥ — the augmentation ideal need no longer be the whole radical, but the radical contribution from a Sylow p-subgroup is nonzero. This is the general Artin–Wedderburn obstruction behind the parent's open question.

crossReferences.description: Extends the parent counterexample (𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is not semisimple, witnessed by the nilpotent g − 1) to the full local-ring structure: g − 1 generates the augmentation ideal, which is nilpotent, equals the Jacobson radical, and makes the algebra local. Completes the parent's first open question (identify g − 1 as a generator of the augmentation ideal) and addresses the radical viewpoint of its second.
Sharpens Maschke's theorem at its modular boundary: the nonzero Jacobson radical of 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is exactly why the char k ∤ |G| hypothesis cannot be dropped.

conclusion.summary: For every prime p, the modular group algebra 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is proved to be a LOCAL ring whose unique maximal ideal is the augmentation ideal ker ε. The augmentation ideal is shown to be PRINCIPAL — ker ε = (g − 1), generated by the nilpotent g − 1 — completing the identification flagged by the parent's first open question; NILPOTENT of index ≤ p — (ker ε)^p = ⊥; MAXIMAL — the kernel of the surjection ε onto the field 𝔽_p; and equal to the JACOBSON RADICAL — Ring.jacobson A = ker ε ≠ ⊥. The nonzero radical gives an independent, radical-theoretic proof that 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] is not semisimple, via the Artinian equivalence IsSemisimpleRing ↔ Ring.jacobson = ⊥. 209 lines, 18 theorems, 3 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: This entry supplies the complete local-ring picture behind the modular failure of Maschke's theorem, beyond the parent's single nilpotent and beyond the sibling's no-complement statement. It establishes that the augmentation ideal is principal (the cyclic-group telescoping g − 1 ∣ gⁿ − 1), nilpotent at the ideal level, the unique maximal ideal, and the Jacobson radical — realizing 𝔽_p[ℤ/p] as the canonical local Artinian ring 𝔽_p[X]/((X − 1)^p). The radical-theoretic non-semisimplicity proof is the form that generalizes to arbitrary finite groups with p ∣ |G|.
openQuestions: Generalize the principal/nilpotent augmentation ideal and locality to 𝔽_p[(ℤ/p)^n] and finite abelian p-groups, with explicit nilpotency index.
For arbitrary finite G with p ∣ |G|, show Ring.jacobson (𝔽_p[G]) ≠ ⊥ via the radical contribution of a Sylow p-subgroup.
